column1: # labels_extcorpus_webpack.tsv — held-out labels for the EXTERNAL-CORPUS slice of the RANKING lane,
# scored against webpack/webpack pinned in bench/recalleval/extcorpus.lock. Driven exactly as
# labels_ranking.tsv is: `--for=<query> --format=candidates`, gold = the 1-based rank of the first
# candidate matching a labelled target. Same 4-column shape, same matcher, same loader — this is not
# a fifth format:
#   query<TAB>primary<TAB>acceptable<TAB>class
#   primary    = comma-separated repo-relative path(s), each optionally `path#SymbolName`. A hit on
#                ANY primary target is primary (strict) credit.
#   acceptable = comma-separated targets earning lenient (graded) credit, or `-` for none.
#   class      = the RETRIEVAL LOSS SHAPE this row exercises, not the query's grammatical shape. The
#                in-tree label files classify by query shape (name/concept/task/adversarial) because
#                they measure the ranker end to end; this slice exists to put a number on four
#                SPECIFIC, separately-diagnosed loss shapes, so per-bucket rates are the whole point
#                and the class column carries the bucket:
#     diagnostic-class     — a conceptual query whose content words are also the NAME of a diagnostic
#                            class (a *Warning / *Error / a plugin that only reports one). The
#                            diagnostic is named after the failure the mechanism can produce, so it
#                            matches the query's words with a tiny body and no competition; the
#                            labelled answer is the MECHANISM, never the diagnostic.
#     thin-registration    — the labelled answer is a small registration/wiring class with near-zero
#                            graph centrality (cx~0, in~0) whose NAME literally spells most of the
#                            query's content words. Structurally central symbols sharing fewer terms
#                            are expected to displace it; this bucket measures whether they do.
#     subsystem-directory  — the concept the query names is the name of a DIRECTORY, and the answer is
#                            the files inside it. Path components are not ranking evidence today, so
#                            the query word matches inside unrelated symbol names elsewhere while the
#                            directory literally named for the concept contributes nothing.
#     vendored-asset       — task-shaped queries whose bundles are polluted by vendored front-end
#                            assets and numbered migrations. webpack carries no row of this class
#                            (that population lives in the django half of the slice); it is named here
#                            only so the two files share one vocabulary.
# LABELING PROTOCOL (held-out means held out, and this file is the honest-fixture case). Every gold
# below was chosen by READING the pinned source at the pinned commit — the file's own body, its class
# and its hooks — and deciding which file IS the on-task answer. NOTHING here was produced by running
# `--for` and transcribing a rank, and the baseline was measured only after this file was complete.
# Provenance is recorded per row in the trailing comment blocks below, split two ways:
#   * OBSERVED  — the query shape came from the competitor head-to-head that first diagnosed the
#                 bucket. Kept because dropping it would discard the only rows with an outside
#                 arm's answer on record. Re-verified against source here regardless.
#   * NEW       — authored in this lane, from source, to keep the slice from being a restatement of
#                 the queries that produced the diagnosis. New rows are the MAJORITY of every bucket
#                 on purpose: a band fitted to the exact set that motivated it measures the fit.
# HONESTY NOTE, stated up front rather than discovered later: `acceptable` is used narrowly. A file
# earns lenient credit only when a competent agent handed THAT file instead of the primary would still
# land the task without another call. Where no such second file exists the column is `-`, even though
# a wider `acceptable` list would flatter every number this file produces.
# Counts: diagnostic-class 8 · thin-registration 8 · subsystem-directory 8 · 24 rows.

# ── PER-ROW PROVENANCE AND THE READING THAT PRODUCED EACH GOLD ────────────────────────────────────
# diagnostic-class
#   OBSERVED "tree shaking … exports as unused" — FlagDependencyUsagePlugin.js imports UsageState from
#     ExportsInfo and drives setUsedConditionally over the module graph; it IS the marking pass. The
#     displacing population at this commit is lib/errors/UnusedReexportsWarning.js,
#     DynamicExportsWarning.js, MissingSideEffectsWarning.js plus their lib/performance/*Plugin.js
#     reporters. ExportsInfo.js is acceptable: it owns UsageState and an agent landing there finds the
#     marking call sites one hop away.
#   OBSERVED "splitChunks produces an empty chunk" — lib/optimize/SplitChunksPlugin.js is the splitter;
#     lib/errors/SplitChunksCappedWarning.js and lib/performance/SplitChunksCappedPlugin.js are the
#     diagnostics named after its failure. RemoveEmptyChunksPlugin.js is acceptable — a genuinely
#     empty chunk is removed there, so an agent handed it can still close the bug.
#   NEW "circular dependencies … detected" — lib/CircularModulesPlugin.js contains CycleGraph and the
#     iterative SCC that finds circular modules ("Detects circular dependencies among synchronous
#     module imports"). lib/errors/CircularDependenciesWarning.js is the diagnostic it constructs.
#   NEW "scope hoisting … cannot be concatenated" — ModuleConcatenationPlugin.js owns BAILOUT_PREFIX,
#     formatBailoutReason and setBailoutReason. lib/errors/ScopeHoistingBailoutsWarning.js and
#     lib/performance/ScopeHoistingBailoutsPlugin.js only report what it decided.
#   NEW "package sideEffects flag" — SideEffectsFlagPlugin.js reads the flag off BuildMeta and rewires
#     Harmony re-export connections. lib/errors/MissingSideEffectsWarning.js is the diagnostic.
#   NEW "maximum size budget" — lib/performance/SizeLimitsPlugin.js holds maxAssetSize/
#     maxEntrypointSize and does the comparison; AssetsOverSizeLimitWarning.js and
#     EntrypointsOverSizeLimitWarning.js are what it emits.
#   NEW "duplicate copies of the same package" — DuplicatePackagesPlugin.js taps thisCompilation/seal/
#     afterSeal and does the grouping; DuplicatePackagesWarning.js is its output. Deliberately kept
#     even though implementation and diagnostic are siblings in one directory: that is the harder
#     case for the bucket, not an easier one.
#   NEW "compile time constants substituted" — DefinePlugin.js's walkDefinitions/walkDefinitionsForValues
#     are the substitution; lib/errors/UnusedDefinesWarning.js + lib/performance/UnusedDefinesPlugin.js
#     are the report.
# thin-registration  (every gold read; each is a single class whose apply() taps one hook)
#   OBSERVED "chunk ids assigned deterministically" — DeterministicChunkIdsPlugin.js, 75 lines.
#   NEW  DeterministicModuleIdsPlugin.js (100) · NamedChunkIdsPlugin.js (94) ·
#        HashedModuleIdsPlugin.js (88) · OccurrenceModuleIdsPlugin.js (179) ·
#        ChunkModuleIdRangePlugin.js (96) · LimitChunkCountPlugin.js (319) · BannerPlugin.js (150).
#        Six of the eight live under lib/ids/, which is also a subsystem-directory population — the
#        two buckets genuinely overlap in this tree and the overlap is not hidden: a fix that only
#        works by lifting the directory would show up in BOTH bucket rates, and the interpretation
#        note in the registration draft says so.
# subsystem-directory
#   OBSERVED "caching layer … new cache backend" — lib/cache/ holds PackFileCacheStrategy.js (1897
#     lines, the on-disk pack format), MemoryCachePlugin.js, IdleFileCachePlugin.js; lib/Cache.js and
#     lib/CacheFacade.js are the API above them. All five read.
#   NEW "module federation" — lib/container/ModuleFederationPlugin.js composes ContainerPlugin and
#     ContainerReferencePlugin; lib/sharing/SharePlugin.js composes Provide/ConsumeSharedPlugin.
#   NEW "objects written into the persistent cache file" — lib/serialization/ObjectMiddleware.js (941)
#     is the object graph walker, FileMiddleware.js the writer, BinaryMiddleware.js the encoder.
#   NEW "hot module replacement runtime applies an update" — lib/hmr/HotModuleReplacement.runtime.js is
#     the runtime itself; HotModuleReplacementRuntimeModule.js (50 lines) only injects it.
#   NEW "css module handling" — lib/css/CssModulesPlugin.js (1281) wires parser and generator;
#     CssParser.js and CssGenerator.js are those two halves.
#   NEW "stats … printable output" — lib/stats/StatsPrinter.js is the printer engine,
#     DefaultStatsPrinterPlugin.js (1774) the format definitions.
#   NEW "umd library wrapper" — lib/library/UmdLibraryPlugin.js extends AbstractLibraryPlugin.
#   NEW "asset module emitted as a separate file" — lib/asset/AssetGenerator.js decides inline vs
#     resource and produces the file; AssetModulesPlugin.js registers the module types.
